title: Kleine stappen, groot verschil: efficiënt aan de slag met digitale toegankelijkheid

Vaak deels omdat je intrinsiek gemotiveerd bent om er voor iedereen te zijn, deels omdat het moet van de wet digitale toegankelijkheid. Toch kan het in de waan van de dag een uitdaging zijn om stappen te zetten. Gelukkig kan je al veel kleine dingen aanpassen in je routine, die een groot verschil maken op lange termijn. title: Art for Everyone: How Public Libraries Expand Access
raw_text: Introducing children to viewing, creating, and enjoying art at a young age helps them appreciate it throughout their lives. Some children are exposed to various forms of art because it is part of their daily life or because they have easy access to museums and galleries in their community. But in many areas across the country, access to museums and art galleries can be cost prohibitive. That is where the public library comes in! While some museums, including the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., offer free admission, millions of people across the country do not have easy access to them. According to the 2024 Annual Survey of Museum-Goers from the American Alliance of Museums and Wilkening Consulting, museum admission costs vary widely, from a few dollars to $40–$50 per adult at some institutions. Among U.S. adults who visit museums at least occasionally, cost was the number one barrier to visiting more often. Among frequent museum-goers, younger adults were twice as likely as seniors to be concerned about admission costs. In response to those barriers, and in an effort to enrich and inspire customers of all ages, many library systems have stepped up to provide access to art in a variety of forms. Borrowing Art from the Library Brooklyn Public Library in New York recently launched a lending program featuring art by local artists. title: 2026 Library Design Showcase
raw_text: Welcome to American Libraries’ 2026 Library Design Showcase, our annual celebration of new and renovated libraries across the US and Canada. The word welcome appeared in many of this year’s submissions, reflecting a growing understanding that in anxious times, the library is a place that should feel good: safe, comfortable, well-lit, plugged in, and deeply connected to its surroundings. More than two-thirds of this year’s 15 selections are renovations or adaptive reuse projects. Libraries of all types are finding ways to acknowledge historical and environmental realities, embrace natural elements and cultural identities, evolve traditions, and build in flexibility to account for the unexpected. Read on for snapshots of these communities in motion. Natural immersion Maplewood (N.J.) Memorial Library Adjacent to a historic park, with protected natural areas on all sides, this 1955 masonry structure had nowhere to expand but up. The new, light-filled second floor features bird-safe glass, wood battens, and green roofs for a treehouse feel. The all-electric building, the first LEED Gold–certified library in New Jersey, includes solar panels that offset more than half of the library’s energy use. title: Secrets of Effective Upskilling
raw_text: This is an excerpt from Upskilling for Library Workers: A Guide for Future-Ready Professionals by Ann Medaille (ALA Editions, 2026). With the advent of new technologies and rapid social and economic shifts, library workers’ jobs are being transformed. Compared with a decade ago, library workers now spend more time consulting on complex research tools, teaching digital literacy classes, supporting virtual learning environments, helping users troubleshoot devices, and codesigning projects with community partners. The pace at which library staffers are called upon to learn new skills is accelerating, and workers may struggle to keep up. In addition, automation and artificial intelligence (AI) are altering many aspects of work. In the long run, technological innovations have the potential to increase productivity and lead to more interesting kinds of work, but in the short term, they often cause disruptions that can be difficult for workers to navigate. To address these changes—and manage the anxieties that come along with them—workers need constant support for skill development. While corporations may embrace upskilling to stay competitive, libraries will have to support upskilling to remain relevant. Library leaders are under greater pressure to respond rapidly to changing social and economic conditions and demonstrate that their libraries make a difference in their communities. title: Hold the Phone
raw_text: Since fall 2024, each school day at Grant High School in Portland, Oregon, has started the same way: Roughly 2,100 students line up to place their phones in gray and green Yondr pouches—the kind live performers use to prevent audience members from recording—as they enter the building. From the morning bell to dismissal, phones are sealed and can be unlocked only with special magnets near the school’s exits as students leave for the day. The high school’s effort to limit phone use on campus has received support from its educators, who say classroom engagement is on the rise, and mixed reviews from students, who dislike being cut off from their devices. But there’s been one unexpected outcome of the policy: More students are spending time in the library, where they’re browsing the collection or hanging out during free periods, says teacher-librarian Paige Battle. “They’re checking out more books, and I feel like that’s been so important in their education,” Battle says. “We’re seeing studies about students, even adults, not having the reading stamina they’ve had in the past, so I’ve been encouraged by this increase.” Roughly six in 10 parents of an 11- or 12-year-old say their child owns a smartphone, according to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey . And as more schools across the country enact phone-free policies—29 states and the District of Columbia have instituted bell-to-bell phone-free policies so far—many school libraries are experiencing a surge in popularity. title: Newsmaker: Min Jin Lee
raw_text: Min Jin Lee has notched career milestones that few authors reach. Her immigration saga Pachinko was both a National Book Award finalist and a New York Times Top 10 Best Book of 2017, and it was adapted into a television series of the same name for Apple TV. Lee is also a Guggenheim fellow and the first Korean American to hold the role of New York State author laureate. Her latest title, American Hagwon (Cardinal, September), examines the influence of Korean “cram schools” among families in the Korean diaspora. American Libraries spoke with Lee ahead of her appearance at the American Library Association’s 2026 Annual Conference and Exhibition in Chicago. She discussed her new book, the library that shaped her, and her antidote to book bans. What inspired you to focus on the education system as it relates to the movements of a middle-class Korean American family in American Hagwon ? My research process involved all these interviews—I’ve done hundreds of them, probably almost 1,000 at this point—and every single time I talked to somebody, they would mention their education path. It was such an important and controversial subject. I thought, if I had to think about the most important value for Koreans, especially in the diaspora, what would I write about? Education turned out to be a beast, because people have lots of feelings about it. In the book, the Koh family loses wealth and status as they weather betrayal and financial crises. title: Mall Wonder
raw_text: After serving its community for nearly 45 years in the same building, Escondido (Calif.) Public Library closed in April 2025 for an $11.6 million renovation. It was important to us, as the city’s lone library, to preserve access during construction. So one month later, our library opened a temporary location in a very different kind of facility: the nearby North County Mall, where services and collections were spread across six storefronts, including a former Abercrombie & Fitch clothing store. Of course, moving a library takes more than a month. Our planning took more than a year and required staff to work under tight deadlines, limited budgets, and high expectations. Here’s how we did it, and what we learned from the process. Choosing a location. It’s essential to consider whether the new location will match, improve upon, or limit access. Retailers and mall operators have already studied traffic patterns, visibility, parking, and nearby amenities. Leverage that knowledge to evaluate access. In our case, the public benefited from a highway and bus stop near the mall, and adjacency to a city park. The arrangement also gave the mall a stable civic tenant and created natural cross-traffic between library patrons and shoppers. The mall was not just available space; it was a location where public access, economic development, and community visibility could overlap. title: Dismantling Disinformation
raw_text: Library workers are well aware of the effects of book bans and censorship. Propaganda and disinformation are the flipside of the same coin. Understanding the complex relationships among these interrelated processes is more critical than ever, especially as libraries explore possible solutions and responses. The following books show how disinformation can lead to censorship and how censorship can, in turn, allow disinformation to thrive. Book Bans, Disinformation, and Cultural Erasure: The Censor­ship Movement in Libraries, Schools, and Society By Paul T. Jaeger Jaeger situates the current book-banning movement within a larger social and political effort to erase marginalized communities and culture. He provides clear definitions and examples of these processes and goals, including the roles played by technological progress and economic inequity. With accessible references (like the Beatles, Dungeons & Dragons, and Holmes and Watson) and nuanced examinations of McCarthyism, the history of libraries, and the myth of neutrality, this is a recommended read for anyone interested in a more expansive understanding of current First Amendment challenges. Bloomsbury Libraries Unlimited, 2026. 320 p. $31.50. 979-8-216-39714-4. (Also available as an ebook.) title: A Sense of Purpose
raw_text: When it comes to building resilient and equitable communities, libraries are natural leaders. We provide places where neighbors meet, learn, and support one another; where sustainability education becomes action; and where residents can find year-round climate refuge. When communities are resilient, they are better able to overcome barriers. The Obama Presidential Center (OPC) branch of Chicago Public Library (CPL) is an example of a library that strengthens the social infrastructure that underpins resilience. CPL Commissioner Chris Brown describes the branch as a civic platform for residents, artists, educators, and organizations to cocreate the life of the library and its surrounding public spaces. Though just 5,000 square feet, OPC was designed to spark connection, invite conversation, and inspire activities that encourage ­socialization and enjoyment. The branch partners with such nonprofits as the Art Institute of Chicago, the literary arts group StoryStudio Chicago , and the artist-led alt_Chicago . OPC is a striking example of how libraries do not just serve resilient communities, they help create them. On the Gulf Coast, sustainability is a daily requirement. Lindsay Cronk, dean of Tulane University Libraries in New Orleans, has shared that the library’s partnership with Keep Louisiana Beautiful , a state program, helps connect students, faculty, and staff with opportunities for conservation, beautification, recycling, and environmental action. title: Googles AI Mode toont minder en vooral duurdere producten
raw_text: Wie via Googles AI Mode naar een product zoekt, krijgt niet alleen veel minder resultaten te zien dan bij een gewone zoekopdracht, maar betaalt voor identieke artikelen ook regelmatig meer. AI Mode is 21,6 procent duurder. Dat blijkt uit nieuw onderzoek van Productrise , een Nederlands analysebedrijf dat zoekresultaten van Google structureel vergelijkt. Ondernemer Hugo Huijer deed 100.000 identieke zoekopdrachten in Search en AI Mode in de maand augustus en komt tot deze verrassende conclusie. Eén productpaar toont in 38 procent van de gevallen een afwijkende prijsstelling, doorgaans in het nadeel van AI Mode. Qua prijsadvies aan de consument is AI een domoor. Er is geen sprake van een spoortje van intelligentie. Huijer tegen Emerce: “Ik kan geen verklaring geven en Google zegt dat het niet zou moeten gebeuren. Toch is het zo. Wat ik kan verzinnen, maar daarvoor heb ik geen bewijsvoering, is dat AI Mode voorrang geeft aan kwaliteit boven kwantiteit. In AI-resultaten amper ruimte voor productaanbevelingen, dus er wordt scherp gekozen.” Wellicht weegt Google achter de schermen factoren als rating van de winkel, verzend- en retoursnelheid en -kosten en voorraadpositie van de betreffende winkel mee. Maar daarover is geen uitsluitsel te geven. Het onderzoek vond plaats in de VS en het VK, omdat AI Mode in die regio’s al enig wezenlijk volume heeft. title: Consumentenstichting SMC: Snapchat houdt verslavend ontwerp in stand
raw_text: Stichting Massaschade & Consument (SMC) heeft vandaag Snap, het bedrijf achter Snapchat, gedagvaard bij de rechtbank Amsterdam vanwege het verslavende ontwerp van de app. Het is voor het eerst dat een Nederlandse rechter over het verslavende ontwerp van sociale apps moet oordelen, na een golf van vergelijkbare zaken in landen als de Verenigde Staten. Snapchat is een berichtenapp die groot werd met foto’s en berichten die na het bekijken vanzelf verdwijnen. Het telt ruim zes miljoen actieve Nederlandse gebruikers en bereikt meer dan 90% van alle 13- tot 24-jarigen. De unieke combinatie van verdwijnende inhoud, zogenoemde streaks en goed getimede meldingen zorgt voor een constante stroom aan app-interacties die de aandacht van gebruikers opeisen. Deze ‘fear of missing out’ werkt volgens de stichting bijzonder effectief. “Verslaving is bij dit soort apps geen bijeffect, maar een verdienmodel”, zegt SMC-voorzitter Lucia Melcherts. “Natuurlijk is Snapchat óók een makkelijke en leuke manier om dagelijks contact te houden met vrienden. Snap heeft er alleen een extra laag overheen gebouwd, die beloont wie elke dag iets stuurt, straft wie een dag overslaat, en dat meteen aan je vrienden laat zien. Zo wordt contact een verplichting met een teller erop: de vriendschap is misschien echt, maar de streak is iets van Snap.” Snap presenteert Snapchat al jaren als de tegenpool van andere sociale platforms: geen likes en volgers, maar ‘echt contact met echte vrienden’. title: Nvidia knuffelt Hugging Face
raw_text: Nvidia neemt het ai-bedrijf Hugging Face over voor 12,9 miljard dollar. In het persbericht daarover is symbolisch een hartje geplaatst tussen de ai-chipleverancier en de community van ontwikkelaars die met open modellen werken. Met de strategische acquisitie versnelt de chipgigant zijn inspanningen om het gebruik van open ai-modellen en -diensten te bevorderen. Samen gaan de bedrijven Hugging Face’s platform uitbreiden, de infrastructuur versterken en de toegang voor ontwikkelaars en instituties wereldwijd vergroten. Meer dan achttien miljoen ontwikkelaars, onderzoekers en ‘creators’ gebruiken dit platform. Ze hebben al meer dan drie miljoen modellen, een half miljoen datasets en een miljoen applicaties gedeeld. De zogenoemde open-weightmodellen van Hugging Face vormen een directe uitdaging voor de gesloten, propriëtaire modellen van Amerikaanse techgiganten zoals OpenAI en Anthropic, maar ook voor goedkope Chinese alternatieven. In tegenstelling tot de duurdere gesloten software zoals die van OpenAI en Anthropic zijn open-weight ai-modellen volledig openbaar. Gebruikers kunnen deze modellen downloaden, finetunen en op hun eigen hardware of servers van derden draaien. Ze mogen de getrainde parameters (de gewichten) lokaal kopiëren en wijzigen. title: ChatGPT-advertenties leveren nog weinig op
raw_text: Veel mediabureaus zien niet de resultaten die ze verwachten van advertentiecampagnes op ChatGPT. Dat gebeurt ondanks de verbeteringen die OpenAI zegt te hebben doorgevoerd om doelgroepen beter te kunnen bereiken. Peter Jaffray, managing director en privacy officer bij het Canadese digitale marketingbureau Choice OMG, vertelde aan MediaPost dat hij een kleinschalige campagne had uitgevoerd gericht op gebruikers in Ontario en Alberta. De campagne leverde geen enkele geïnteresseerde koper op. Volgens Jaffray waren de advertenties wel daadwerkelijk vertoond en waren de kosten laag. De advertenties bereiken momenteel alleen gebruikers van de gratis versie van ChatGPT, aldus Jaffray. Hij besteedde in totaal 415 dollar aan drie campagnes. OpenAI begon pas in augustus 2026 met het aanbieden van mogelijkheden voor geografische targeting en aangepaste doelgroepen. Tegelijkertijd introduceerde het bedrijf functies voor conversie-optimalisatie, de OpenAI Pixel Conversions API en metingen door externe partijen. Ook Nicholas Verity, CEO van B2B-leadgeneratiebureau Cleverly, testte onlangs advertenties op ChatGPT, maar is daarmee opgehouden. Net als Jaffray zag hij redelijke click-throughpercentages, maar geen enkele conversie. Volgens Verity kwamen de cijfers niet overeen met de werkelijkheid. Hij stelde dat er mogelijk iets mis is met de meetgegevens of dat klikken van dezelfde gebruiker dubbel worden geteld. Daardoor zag hij geen reden om meer geld in de campagnes te steken. title: Competitive Pokémon is on phones now, but you still need a Switch to become a champion
raw_text: To get started with competitive Pokémon battles, all you need is your phone. But to compete at the highest level, like at the Pokémon World Championships, you're going to need a Switch. And there doesn't seem to be a good reason why. Battle simulator Pokémon Champions originally launched on the Switch and Switch 2 in April, with the mobile version following in June. The experience is nearly identical across the game's versions; since it's cross-platform, the choice really comes down to what devices you own and whether you prefer tapping or using a controller. title: Explore the globe in field recordings
raw_text: Around the world in 80 WAVs. | Screenshot: Terrence O’Brien / The Verge I love field recordings. I love making them. I love them when they're incorporated into my ambient music . They're great background noise for working or sleeping. But they're also great for active listening, focusing in on the fine nuances of burbling brooks or urban chaos. Earth Garden gives you a globe to explore with real field recordings taken from various locations. Earth Garden is inspired by Radio Garden (which you should also check out) except, instead of exploring the world via radio, it's environmental sounds. title: iPhone Handoff will seamlessly share one number between two phones
raw_text: When iOS 27 lands later this month, it will have a feature called iPhone Handoff that lets you switch between two phones using the same number. It was briefly mentioned during the WWDC keynote back in June, but there were no details at the time. Now there's a demo clip showing how to set up the feature running in Xcode 27's Device Hub. It lets you pair two iPhones, using one as your main device and the other as its " companion ." Launching the feature now makes sense with the expected launch of the foldable iPhone Ultra right around the corner . title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
raw_text: There’s some real gems in there. | Photo: Terrence O’Brien / The Verge According to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), CD sales exploded in the first half of 2026. A new report from the organization says 17.5 million CDs were sold in the first six months of the year, up from just 12 million during the same period in 2025. That's a jump of 45.7 percent, and 58.6 percent in dollars, which reached $171.1 million. What makes this all the more shocking is that CD sales actually shrank 22 percent from 2024 to 2025.
